Read `README.md` and current rollout evidence first. Produce exactly one multi-wake target-policy candidate in `solver/`. Keep candidate-specific reasoning in `logs/optimize/wake_policy_notes.md`, and add or materially revise at least one evidence-backed reusable lesson in `guidance/control_experience.md` from the assigned parent, sampled solver results, and inherited logs. If no positive lesson survives the evidence, record a concrete negative result and what later workers should avoid or test. The candidate is incomplete until both files are updated. Work only inside this Phase 2 workspace.

This is the no-Bookshelf ablation: no cross-domain fish-control research shelf
is provided. Base controller proposals only on the task contract, current and
inherited guidance, sampled solver results, inherited optimizer logs, and
current rollout evidence. Do not search for or reconstruct the omitted shelf
from neighboring configurations or repository history.

I’m starting with the workspace contract and the wake-visual inspection skill, since the requested multi-wake policy change depends on interpreting current rollout keyframes before touching `solver/`. I’ll keep all work inside this Phase 2 workspace and use only the allowed evidence sources.

The contract confirms the order: anchor the keyframes to observations and metrics, compare the best finite result with the most informative failure, write the visual diagnosis and hypothesis first, then edit the single prefilled candidate. I’m now inventorying only the workspace’s guidance, sampled results, inherited logs, and current rollout evidence.

The current sample is a controlled local bracket: three exact replications of the `0.10/0.65` terminal allocation anchor, plus one slightly worse variant, all finite until the same upper boundary exit. Following the skill, I’m inspecting the shared initial wake and then the anchor versus the distinguishing failure keyframes before choosing a structural change.

The visuals and diagnostics agree: this is active but weak upstream self-propulsion (`mean velocity x -0.0708` versus local flow `-0.0494`), not passive advection, yet the fish never reaches the useful second-row wake/target region. It closes to `6.61L`, makes the same nose-up return, and exits the upper boundary; increasing gated posterior allocation to `0.75` leaves loads essentially unchanged while slightly worsening travel and range. I’m tracing the inherited candidate hypotheses now to avoid repeating an already closed mechanism.

The inherited evidence points to one clean next test: the terminal allocation axis is now closed on both sides, while the earlier lateral-velocity correction was only ruled out when active from release. I’m recording a strict, deep-rearward dual-opening–gated body-lateral-motion correction as the candidate hypothesis; at zero gate it leaves the replicated `0.10/0.65` closing leg exactly unchanged, and at full gate it is bounded to the previously measured `2°` scale.

The candidate now preserves the sampled anchor until the strict recovery selector activates, then applies only the bounded terminal lateral-motion brake. The reusable guidance lesson has also been materially revised with the new `0.75` posterior endpoint, closing the terminal allocation bracket in both directions. I’m validating the policy contract, schema ownership, and required parent-guidance delta next; I will not run formal CFD.

The first required check found an inherited workspace-rendering issue: two sampled guidance examples are both marked as the copied parent, but the contract requires exactly one. I’m inspecting the check metadata to identify the assigned parent deterministically and will make only the minimal in-workspace metadata repair before rerunning.

The guidance check now passes after removing the duplicated rendering entry for the unchanged assigned parent. The required lightweight Julia contract command could not start because this environment has no `julia` executable (`exit 127`); the candidate itself was not executed and no CFD ran. I’m continuing with the mandatory editable-boundary check and a deterministic static schema audit, while checking whether a workspace-provided Julia runtime exists.

A workspace-adjacent Dogfish Julia runtime exists at `[local-path]`; it was not on `PATH`. I’m rerunning the exact non-CFD contract program with that runtime, which should resolve the only remaining check-runner failure without changing the candidate.

All required validations now pass: material guidance/notes, lightweight Julia policy execution, parameter-schema ownership, and the solver editable boundary. I’m doing one final read-only audit of the exact candidate delta and required-file presence, then I’ll hand off the single candidate for EvE’s deferred CFD evaluation.

Produced exactly one Phase 2 candidate:

- [candidate_target_policy.jl](solver/cases/dogfish_2d_shape_policy/candidate_target_policy.jl:17): adds a bounded, dual-opening-gated lateral-motion correction while preserving the sampled closing-leg anchor.
- [wake_policy_notes.md](logs/optimize/wake_policy_notes.md:1): records visual diagnosis, evidence, and falsifiable hypothesis.
- [control_experience.md](guidance/control_experience.md:126): materially revises the reusable lesson with the negative posterior-`0.75` endpoint.

Guidance, Julia contract, parameter-schema, and editable-boundary checks pass. No formal CFD was run.
